fix_commit_message:
avformat/mxfdec: Check edit_unit for being larger than signed 64bit

Fixes: signed integer overflow: 2 * -4962931467012268000 cannot be represented in type 'long'
Fixes: 376496313/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_dem_MXF_fuzzer-4921469185884160

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix f7cc023f06c4 on top of intro 649ac17efd96 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (IntegerOverflow): In FFmpeg's MXF demuxer, mxf_edit_unit_absolute_offset() rescales and clamps a caller-supplied edit_unit value against the bounds of the index table's first/last segments. The clamp only bounds edit_unit between first_segment->index_start_position and index_end but does not verify the result is non-negative. A maliciously crafted MXF file can set an index table segment's IndexStartPosition to an extremely large negative int64 value, causing the clamped edit_unit to also be an extreme negative value. This value is later used to compute `index = edit_unit - s->index_start_position`, and for certain (Avid-style) VBR indexes the code executes `index *= 2`, which overflows signed 64-bit arithmetic when the input is close to INT64_MIN, triggering undefined behavior caught by the UBSan-instrumented fuzzer. Root cause: The refactored fast-path clamp added in the 'Speed up mxf_edit_unit_absolute_offset()' commit clamps edit_unit's upper and lower bound using index metadata read directly from the file, without validating the sign/range of the resulting edit_unit before it is used in subsequent signed integer arithmetic (including a multiplication by 2 for Avid-style indexes).
